subject: Helios RFP: model supply traceability & attestation questionnaire
messages:
From: Helena Black <helena.black@heliosfinancial.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@heliosfinancial.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Helios RFP: Model supply traceability & attestation (Section C)

Rishi,

Thanks for taking this — attached is Section C of our RFP which drills into model supply chain, licensing, and provenance. We need a formal response covering:

- Model origin attestations (source repo, commit id or snapshot) for cataloged models
- License mappings and compatibility for derivative/customized artifacts
- Version pinning and update/rollback policy (how we are notified; windows; automation)
- SBOM-style artifact export (list of dependencies, tokenizer, any compiled kernels)
- Data retention / logs for provenance audits

Can you confirm if Redwood can provide an attestation letter or signed checklist and a sample SBOM export by June 3? If an on-call / working session is helpful, we can schedule a 30-min call this week.

Helena Black
Head of Vendor Risk, Helios Financial
helena.black@heliosfinancial.com
Attachments: Helios_RFP_Section-C_Model_Traceability.pdf
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Helena Black <helena.black@heliosfinancial.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Helios RFP: Model supply traceability & attestation (Section C)

Helena —

Appreciate the clear ask and the deadline. We can provide a formal attestation plus a machine-readable SBOM extract. I'm attaching our draft RFI response (sectioned to match your PDF) so you can see the level of detail. Highlights here:

- Model origin: For each verified model in the Redwood catalog we record source repo/url, published artifact digest (SHA256), and the model snapshot ID used for serving. For models we host that originated from third parties, we include the upstream release tag and snapshot time.
- License mapping: We maintain per-model license metadata (SPDX where available) and a compatibility summary for common enterprise use-cases; our legal team notes any restrictions for commercial redistribution or derivative training.
- Pinning & updates: Customers can pin to a specific catalog snapshot id (immutable) or to a channel (e.g., stable/latest). We provide change logs and a 7-day advance notification window for non-critical model updates; critical security patches are rolled with post-facto notices and optional automatic pin-hold.
- SBOM: We can deliver CSV/JSON SBOM exports that enumerate tokenizer code, model weights artifact id, quantization metadata, and runtime kernel versions.
- Audit logs: All deployment and pinning events are retained for 3 years by default; exportable audit trail available for compliance review.

We'll circle back with a signed attestation doc and a SBOM sample. Would a short call Wednesday at 10am PT work to go over any edge cases?

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Trust & Compliance (acting)
Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Helios RFP: Model supply traceability & attestation (internal draft)

Team —

Looping you in to review my draft answers before I send the formal attestation to Helios. Key open items:

1) License nuance on model forks: Priyom, can you confirm the language we should use for cases where an upstream model is Apache-2.0 but a downstream variant contains GPL-licensed tokenizer tooling? I've penciled: "We surface SPDX license tags for both model artifact and ancillary tooling; where incompatibilities exist we flag them and provide mitigation options (isolation, commercial license, or removal)" — is that safe?

2) Pinning automation: Marissa — product question: we currently offer a 7-day advance notification for non-breaking updates. For enterprise Dedicated/Private customers we support configurable windowing (0-30 days) and automatic safe-rollback to the prior snapshot if a new variant exceeds a quality threshold. Can you confirm the rollback metric and the default rollback window?

3) SBOM export format: Neha — sample CSV attached (SBOM-sample.csv) showing fields we can export. Can we confirm the retention policy stated (3 years) is okay from legal?

Please review and reply with edits; aim for final by Tuesday EOD so we can sign and return to Helios by June 3.

—R

Attachments: SBOM-sample.csv
From: Helena Black <helena.black@heliosfinancial.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Helios RFP: Model supply traceability & attestation

Rishi —

Thanks for the quick reply and the draft. A couple of clarifications from our risk team:

- Automatic repinning: we want assurance that Helios can opt out of automatic repinning and that Redwood will not silently switch a pinned workload to a new artifact. Does your "pin to channel" option ever auto-migrate pinned snapshots?
- Notification windows: the 7-day advance notice is acceptable for non-breaking updates. For security-critical fixes, what is your notification cadence and the option to delay or control deployment?
- Signed attestation: will Redwood sign a one-page attestation on company letterhead confirming the SBOM and provenance fields you listed?

If you can confirm those three points and attach the signed attestation, we can mark Section C as satisfied.

Helena
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Helena Black <helena.black@heliosfinancial.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 17:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Helios RFP: Model supply traceability & attestation — signed attestation and SBOM

Helena —

Thanks for the clarifying questions. Short answers below followed by attachments and links:

1) Automatic repinning: Customers who pin to an immutable snapshot id are never auto-migrated. The "channel" option (e.g., stable/latest) is a convenience string that we may update when a new snapshot is promoted, but any customer who has pinned to an explicit snapshot id will remain on that artifact until they choose to update. We do not silently switch pinned snapshots.

2) Notification cadence for security fixes: For critical security patches that affect served artifacts (e.g., vulnerability in a tokenizer library or a dependency used in weight loading), Redwood uses a two-step process: immediate notification to the customer security contact (email + Console alert) within 2 hours of triage, and a remediation window recommendation within 24 hours. Customers can opt to defer automatic deployment; for Dedicated and Private customers we will hold automated updates until explicit approval.

3) Signed attestation: Attached is a one-page attestation on Redwood letterhead (PDF) that confirms the provenance fields we provide, our SBOM export capability, and the retention policy for audit logs. If Helios needs an executed (wet-signature) copy we can route through DocuSign (I've included a DocuSign placeholder link).

Additional resources:
- Model catalog report (verified entries): https://app.redwood.ai/models/catalog/verified#model-catalog-report
- Shared RFI answers and document pack: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/Helios-HLS-2027-049/RFI-answers

Attachments: Redwood_Attestation_Helios_HLS-2027-049.pdf, RFI_Redwood_Model-Catalog_Attestation.docx, SBOM-sample.csv

Let me know if you want a quick call tomorrow to walk through the attestation. We're aligned to get this signed and returned.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
